rationale: Standard and Fast share explicit opt-in for fixed FP64 J/K/range-K anchors in eligible WB97M-V restricted exact-Direct cold nonlocal outer solves. Unset and 0 keep the incumbent path for both profiles; 1 requests the same scientifically admitted bounded optimization, without a fixed AO ceiling. FP64 eligibility follows actual arithmetic rather than the presence of an application budget. The previous Fast-only automatic floor is withdrawn rather than promoting an incompletely qualified Standard default. This conservative shared policy makes no speedup claim and may give up previously measured Fast savings. Provisional linear operators consume total current-minus-anchor density; full targets refresh FP64 anchors and nonlinear XC/VV10 retain total density. Unsupported models, DF/UKS, warm solves, chunk or public resource-ledger owners and optional device-allocation failures retain their incumbent paths. Five FP64 matrices and one scalar remain charged and can be retired before forces without revoking the final physical state. Numerical acceptance gates are unchanged.
revisit_condition: A common automatic policy requires matched Standard/Fast complete cold/warm/moved energy/force endpoints, independent oracles, semantic work counts, bounded resource/failure evidence and profitable endpoint measurements. Historical Standard-only or Fast-only measurements do not qualify a shared default. Preserve explicit rollback, strict full-target closure and force-phase optional-memory fallback.
